findings.claim: The done check bans any path that does not exist here, but kept rules scope themselves with paths: globs for directories planned tickets will create (plugin/**, docs/**, src/kmctl/cli/**, src/kmctl/hooks/**, .github/workflows/**). Read literally, the check forces those globs out, so the rules for the plugin, docs and CLI would not load when claude-plugin, write-docs-skill and ci-action create those files. The plan must say whether a glob for a planned directory counts, and the grep must not flag it.

The done check bans the word loopctl, but this repo runs its own tickets through loopctl (.loop/config.toml, AGENTS.md's Gates section, the plugin hooks). A kept rule that tells agents to write .loop/ only through loopctl would be true here and still fail the grep. The plan must decide: either rules about the loop workflow are out of scope (left to the loop-harness plugin, and the rules that describe loopctl internals, such as artifact-outputs.md and data-management.md, get deleted), or the check allows loopctl where a rule means the tool this repo uses.
The plan now allows paths: globs for plugin/, docs/, src/kmctl/ and .github/workflows/, so the done check no longer pushes the builder to strip rule scoping for planned folders.
The loopctl ban is gone; a kept rule may name loopctl as the tool this repository's tickets run on, and the loop workflow is handed to the loop-harness plugin.

The path clause still fails the OKF bundle sections that kmctl's own manifesto defines but that do not exist yet: .okf/architecture/, practices/, proposals/, prototypes/, handoffs/. Today .okf/ holds only decisions/, index.md, log.md and manifesto.md. diagrams-stay-current is about `.okf/architecture/`, okf-bundle lists the sections (and the briefing ticket builds its shipped rules from okf-bundle and docs-layout), docs-layout names `.okf/prototypes/<name>/` and `.okf/proposals/`, and cli-interface, cli-version-floor and skills-are-thin cite `.okf/architecture/cli-and-plugin.md`. Read as written, the check makes the builder delete these true references or drop diagrams-stay-current, the same problem as p1 in a different folder. Fix: allow paths under the .okf/ sections the manifesto names (manifesto.md lines 41-42), and say whether a cited page that does not exist yet, like cli-and-plugin.md, should be dropped or kept.
Planned folders (plugin/, docs/, src/kmctl/, .github/workflows/) stay allowed in paths globs and rule text.
A kept rule may name loopctl as this repository's ticket tool; the loop workflow belongs to the plugin.

The plan now lists the manifesto's .okf/ sections (architecture/, practices/, proposals/, prototypes/, handoffs/) and the root action.yml as planned locations, and says a citation of a specific page that does not exist yet (such as cli-and-plugin.md) is dropped.

diagrams-stay-current requires a `depicts:` front-matter field on every diagram, but OKF v0.2 does not define it and no ADR names it; ADR 0009 says any extension field other than handoff_key needs its own ADR, and okf-bundle.md restates that kmctl uses only spec fields plus ADR-named ones.

measure-before-ticketing says a measurement spike is `loopctl plan spike` with its scripts kept in the spike (under .loop/), while docs-layout says a spike goes to .okf/ and that every script producing a number lives in .okf/prototypes/<name>/. The two kept rules give different homes for the same measurement.

entries.change: Diagrams list what they depict in a Depicts body section instead of a depicts front matter field, so no unnamed OKF extension field.
A plan-risk spike stays in .loop/ through loopctl plan spike; analysis behind a cited number is a prototype in .okf/prototypes/<name>/.
The audience constraint now names prototypes for .okf/ and says a plan-risk spike stays with its ticket in .loop/, matching measure-before-ticketing.
